column7: STAND-IN FINGERING: Almenraeder 1824 'Abhandlung ueber die Verbesserung des Fagotts', Tabelle II (a 15-key instrument of 1824, used for an 18-key instrument of c. 1840-50), left table column 5 ('d' after 'des', solfege re), rows R1, R2 and R4 open (open circles; the plate prints no legend: filled = closed is INFERRED from column 1, Bb1, filled in every row), every other left row closed; heading 1 of the plate: every hole of the right-drawn system closed for these columns. Row identity PROBABLE, by order along the drawn instrument from the bell: R1 = bell low-B hole (hole 23), R2 = c1 (22), R4 = d1 (20); R3 = low C# (21), R5 = low Eb (19), R6 = e1 (18), R7 = f1 (17) closed; R8 to R10 closed (identity unknown); holes with no plate row (Bb x2, F# x2, A up, Ab x2, C# x2, g, the three finger holes of the wing, boot c and b) take the REST STATE closed, which the Heckel1 sheets do not show: DECLARED.
